problem: 0060C038 family (49 members, 22 words each): original stores a blx-dispatched virtual-call result via `mov r1,r0; str r1,[r4,#0x818]`; every b1049 source variant emits `str r0,[r4,#0x818]` (21/22 words, similarity 93%, no other diff).
construct: No source construct found. Mechanism, now measured rather than guessed: b1049 DOES emit `mov r1,r0; str r1,[off]` after an INDIRECT `blx` call, but only when the call result must stay live across an instruction that clobbers r0 before its single store. Reproducer (verified): `u8* f(u8* a0, Fns* ft){ u8* p=(u8*)ft->alloc(0x40); *(u32*)p=(u32)a0; *(s32*)(p+0x10)=ft->getval(p,"CLR1"); return p; }` compiles to `BLX r2; MOV r1,r0; MOV r0,r5; STR r1,[r5,#0x10]` (the r0 clobber is the function's own return-value setup `mov r0,r5`, scheduled before the store). The same shape appears for a direct BL (p2: `BL getval; MOV r1,r0; MOV r0,r4; STR r1,[r4,#0x10]`). A second use of the result (e.g. passing it to a later call) also produces `mov r1,r0`, but then the store keeps r0 (`BLXr1 MOVr1,r0 STRr0,[r4,#0x818] MOVr0,r4 BLsink`), so it does not give the target pairing. In 0060C038 there is no second use and no live-in clobber, so the copy in the original can only be the residue of a pre-RA schedule in which the store was deferred past the `ldrb r0,[r4,#0x861]` flag load (the final scheduler then hoisted the store back in front of it): the target's own order is `mov r1,r0 / str r1,[r4,#0x818] / ldrb r0,[r4,#0x861]`, i.e. the value ends in r1 while r0 is reused by the flag load. The parked note's premise ('b1049 emits it only for direct BL') is refuted by the reproducer above. NOTE for whoever picks this up: the rest of the function is fully pinned. It matches word-for-word only when the request call is written with an aliasing local: `if (p->flag861) { Npc* q = p; q->request(q->request854, -1); }` (writing `p->request(p->request854,-1)` makes armcc emit `ldr r0,[r4]` first instead of `ldr r1,[r4]`, a 4-word diff).

Large-but-simplifying inline setter bodies meant to force LATE inlining (12 shapes: extra locals, arrays, nested structs, `if (a==a)`, `for(i<1)`, `switch(0)`, nested blocks, `do{}while(0)`): every one is substituted early - `BLX r1; STR r0,[r4,#0x818]`.

Two byte loads (flag + request854) forced before the store in both orders: armcc hoists both loads into the header block and still keeps the call result in r0 (`BLXr1; LDRB r2,[r4,#0x861]; LDRB r1,[r4,#0x854]; STR r0,[r4,#0x818]; CMP r2,#0`), so extra register pressure alone never displaces the result.

Decisive negative: no instruction in the header block of this function *requires* r0 (only the flag `ldrb`, which the allocator is free to put in r1/r2, and it does). b1049 only forces the result out of r0 when a fixed-r0 user exists in the block (argument setup `mov r0,rX` or the function's return-value setup, as in the reproducer). The original's orphan `mov r1,r0` therefore implies such an r0-requiring instruction existed before register allocation and was deleted afterwards; no tested source produces that state.
